finding.claim: Claim validators (aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce, and iat for maxAge) are skipped when the claim is absent from the payload, so a validly signed token that omits the claim passes the configured allowlist unless the claim is also listed in requiredClaims.
finding.source: Precondition: a token validly signed with the verifier's key that lacks aud/iss/sub/jti/nonce/iat (e.g. issued for another audience or service sharing the key, or issued with noTimestamp for maxAge).
finding.sink: Accept decision: verify() returns the payload (verifier.js:426 sync, verifier.js:471 async) for a token whose claim the operator meant to constrain.

trace.note: validateAlgorithmAndSignature enforces alg allowlist and signature, so the token must be genuinely signed
requiredClaims presence check runs only if the option is set
validators loop over configured claim checks
if (!(claim in payload)) continue; absent claim skips the allowlist/maxAge check
allowedJti/aud/iss/sub/nonce validators are built only from options
maxAge validator checks iat; skipped when iat is absent

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification (verifier.js:169), alg allowlist (verifier.js:162), requiredClaims (verifier.js:293, opt-in only), type checks (verifier.js:316). exp/nbf absence is by design and not reported. Severity depends on whether the operator also sets requiredClaims.

finding.claim: Cache TTL ignores exp when the token has no iat, so a token whose exp has passed is still served from cache until cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after it was first verified.
finding.source: Precondition: the verifier has caching enabled, and the token has exp but no iat (e.g. signer option noTimestamp: true, or an external issuer). The token was successfully verified once before exp.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return of an expired token's payload from verify() (verifier.js:376-377 via handleCachedResult).

trace.note: cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) on each call
hasIat is false for a token without iat
exp-derived cacheValue[2] is set only inside the hasIat block, so it stays 0
cacheValue[2] = maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL
hit check uses only min/max; exp is not re-evaluated
now <= max holds until cacheTTL elapses, so the expired token hits

finding.guards_checked: Cache is opt-in (createCache returns null when cache is unset, verifier.js:84-85). The uncached path does enforce exp (verifier.js:304-323), so the inconsistency exists only on cache hits. Cache key is the full token string, so no cross-token confusion.

finding.claim: Cached inactive (nbf in the future) errors do not record nbf, so a token rejected as not-yet-active stays rejected until errorCacheTTL elapses, even after nbf has passed.
finding.source: Precondition: caching enabled with a positive errorCacheTTL (default -1 at verifier.js:499). A token presented before its nbf.
finding.sink: Cached TokenError returned from verify() on later calls (verifier.js:141-147 handleCachedResult).

trace.note: TokenError values take the early-return branch
cacheValue[2] = now + tolerance + errorCacheTTL; cacheValue[1] (min) is never set
cache lookup returns the error with min=0
hit while now <= max, regardless of nbf

finding.guards_checked: Opt-in cache and errorCacheTTL. Availability-only impact; no authorization bypass.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, passing a Buffer token makes the default cacheKeyBuilder throw a TypeError synchronously, before decode and before any callback/promise handling.
finding.source: Caller-supplied token of type Buffer, which the type check explicitly accepts (verifier.js:353).
finding.sink: hashToken calls token.split (utils.js:46); Buffer has no split, so the exception escapes verify() itself.

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted
cache is enabled
cacheKeyBuilder(token) with default hashToken
token.split('.', 1) on a Buffer throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 accepts Buffers. Not reached: decode(), since the throw happens earlier. Impact is a thrown exception (possible crash or 500 for callers that do not wrap verify), not an auth bypass. Only with the default cacheKeyBuilder.

finding.claim: Signature segment accepts non-canonical base64url (non-zero padding bits), so one valid signature has several distinct token strings; the code comment claims canonical signatures.
finding.source: Attacker holds one valid token and alters the last base64url character of the signature segment.
finding.sink: Raw-token-string identity used by consumers for replay/one-time-use or revocation keyed on the full token string.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE only checks the alphabet, not canonical trailing bits
signatureSegment passes the alphabet check
Buffer.from(signature,'base64') ignores non-zero trailing bits, so variant strings decode to the same bytes
timingSafeEqual passes for every variant (HS256: 4 variant strings)
comment asserts signature is canonical; it is not

finding.guards_checked: Signature is cryptographically correct (timingSafeEqual, crypto.js:391). The malleability does not affect the signed input, which is the raw header.payload string. Only consumers that key replay or revocation on the raw token string are affected. jti-based checks are unaffected.

finding.claim: Public JWK/JWKS detection runs only if the trimmed key starts with '{' or '[', and trim() does not strip control characters such as U+0000-U+0008 or zero-width U+200B, so a public JWK with such a prefix is accepted as an HMAC secret.
finding.source: Precondition: the key option is public JWK JSON text carrying a leading control or zero-width character (e.g. from a DB or JWKS store), with an HS* algorithm allowed.
finding.sink: HMAC key derivation (createSecretKey via prepareKeyOrSecret, verifier.js:550 / signer.js:241), reopening the GHSA-g3jj public-JWK-as-secret class.

trace.note: performDetectPrivateKeyAlgorithm trims the key
locatePem finds no PEM header in a JWK
isRawSecret branch
isAsymmetricJwkJson returns false when firstChar is not { or [
same trim-then-first-char gap in performDetectPublicKeyAlgorithms

finding.guards_checked: JWK kty check (crypto.js:85-87, 110-114), PEM locator (crypto.js:123-131). Defense-in-depth gap; needs the operator to supply such key text, so reachability is low.

finding.claim: additionalHeader is spread after alg/typ/kid, so the header option can override alg, making the token header disagree with the algorithm used to sign.
finding.source: The header option (developer-supplied). Only exploitable if that option is built from client input.
finding.sink: Emitted token header; signature is made with the configured algorithm (signer.js:126, 167).

trace.note: header.alg = algorithm
...additionalHeader overrides alg, typ, kid
signature uses configured algorithm, not header.alg

finding.guards_checked: Verifier rejects a mismatched header alg (verifier.js:162), so this produces an unverifiable token rather than a forgery. Informational.
